# `silk/semver/range`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Version ranges in the npm and Cargo syntaxes: parse a requirement and test versions against it.

## When to use

Use [`VersionRange.parseNpm`](#VersionRange.impl.parseNpm) for ranges from `package.json`, such as `^1.2.3 || >=2.1.0 <3`,
and [`VersionRange.parseCargo`](#VersionRange.impl.parseCargo) for requirements from `Cargo.toml`, such as `>=1.2, <1.5`. Then
call [`VersionRange.matches`](#VersionRange.impl.matches) for each version, or [`VersionRange.bestMatch`](#VersionRange.impl.bestMatch) to pick the
highest one that matches.

## Details

A [`VersionRange`](#VersionRange) borrows its text and does not allocate. Parsing checks the whole text, and
each match reads the text again, so a match costs time in proportion to the length of the range.

The two syntaxes give different meanings to the same text:

| Text | npm | Cargo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `1.2.3` | exactly `1.2.3` | `^1.2.3` |
| `^1.2.3` | `>=1.2.3, <2.0.0` | `>=1.2.3, <2.0.0` |
| `~1.2.3` | `>=1.2.3, <1.3.0` | `>=1.2.3, <1.3.0` |
| `1.2.x`, `1.2.*` | `>=1.2.0, <1.3.0` | `>=1.2.0, <1.3.0` |
| `>=1 <2`, `>=1, <2` | space means AND | comma means AND |
| `a || b` | either range | not valid |
| `1.0.0 - 2.0.0` | `>=1.0.0, <=2.0.0` | not valid |

In both syntaxes, a pre-release version such as `1.3.0-beta` matches only if a comparator of the
range names a pre-release of the same `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. So `^1.2.3` does not match
`1.3.0-beta`, but `>=1.3.0-alpha` matches `1.3.0-beta`. Use
[`VersionRange.matchesIncludingPrerelease`](#VersionRange.impl.matchesIncludingPrerelease) to drop that rule.

## Gotchas

The npm parser follows the strict mode of the `semver` package: loose forms such as `01.2.3` or
`1.2.3beta` are errors. Build metadata in a range is accepted only after a full version, and it
does not change the result.

## Examples

### Pick the newest compatible version

```silk
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.semver.range { VersionRange }
import silk.semver.version { Version, SemverError }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let range = match VersionRange.parseNpm("^1.2.0") {
    Result<VersionRange, SemverError>.Success { value } => value
    Result<VersionRange, SemverError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  let versions = [Version.make(1, 1, 9), Version.make(1, 4, 2), Version.make(2, 0, 0)]
  return match range.bestMatch(&versions) {
    Option<usize>.Some { value } => {
      if value != 1 {
        return 1
      }
      return 0
    }
    Option<usize>.None => 1
  }
}
```

<a id="VersionRange"></a>

## `VersionRange`

```silk
pub struct VersionRange<'text>
```

A parsed version range that borrows its text.

### Details

Make one with [`VersionRange.parseNpm`](#VersionRange.impl.parseNpm) or [`VersionRange.parseCargo`](#VersionRange.impl.parseCargo). The value is `Copy`,
does not allocate, and cannot live longer than its text. Each match reads the text again, so it
costs time in proportion to the length of the range.

A pre-release version matches only if a comparator of the range names a pre-release of the same
`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. [`VersionRange.matchesIncludingPrerelease`](#VersionRange.impl.matchesIncludingPrerelease) drops that rule.

<a id="VersionRange.impl.parseNpm"></a>

### Associated function `parseNpm`

```silk
pub fn parseNpm(text: string<'text>) -> Result<VersionRange<'text>, SemverError>
```

Parses a range in the npm syntax of the `semver` package, such as `^1.2.3 || >=2.1.0 <3`.

#### Details

`||` separates alternatives, and spaces separate comparators that must all match. Each
comparator is one of these forms. `M`, `m`, and `p` are numbers, and any of them can be `x`,
`X`, or `*`, or be left out, to match any value.

- `1.2.3` or `=1.2.3`: exactly that version. `1.2` means `>=1.2.0 <1.3.0`, and `*` or empty
  text means any version.
- `>1.2.3`, `>=1.2.3`, `<1.2.3`, `<=1.2.3`: comparisons. A partial version counts as its range,
  so `<=1.2` means `<1.3.0` and `>1.2` means `>=1.3.0`.
- `^1.2.3`: changes that do not modify the leftmost nonzero number, `>=1.2.3 <2.0.0`. `^0.2.3`
  means `>=0.2.3 <0.3.0`, and `^0.0.3` means `>=0.0.3 <0.0.4`.
- `~1.2.3` or `~>1.2.3`: patch changes, `>=1.2.3 <1.3.0`. `~1` means `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`.
- `1.2.3 - 2.3.4`: inclusive, `>=1.2.3 <=2.3.4`. A partial upper end counts as its range, so
  `1.2.3 - 2.3` means `>=1.2.3 <2.4.0`.

An operator can have spaces after it, and a version can have a `v` prefix. Upper bounds made
from partial versions exclude the pre-releases of the bound, so `^1.2.3` does not match
`2.0.0-rc.1`.

#### Errors

- `SemverError` with the reason and byte offset of the first problem, such as
  `UnexpectedCharacter` for an unknown operator or a single `|`, `LeadingZero` for `01`, and
  `UnexpectedEnd` for an operator with no version after it.

#### Gotchas

A bare `1.2.3` matches only `1.2.3` in npm, but means `^1.2.3` in Cargo. Loose forms that the
`semver` package accepts only with its `loose` option, such as `01.2.3`, are errors.

<a id="VersionRange.impl.parseCargo"></a>

### Associated function `parseCargo`

```silk
pub fn parseCargo(text: string<'text>) -> Result<VersionRange<'text>, SemverError>
```

Parses a requirement in the Cargo syntax, such as `>=1.2, <1.5` or `0.4`.

#### Details

Commas separate comparators that must all match. Each comparator is an optional operator and a
version, where the minor and patch numbers can be left out:

- `1.2.3` or `^1.2.3`: changes that do not modify the leftmost nonzero number, `>=1.2.3,
  <2.0.0`. `^0.2.3` means `>=0.2.3, <0.3.0`, `^0.0.3` means `=0.0.3`, and `^0` means `<1.0.0`.
- `~1.2.3`: patch changes, `>=1.2.3, <1.3.0`. `~1` means `>=1.0.0, <2.0.0`.
- `=1.2.3`, `>1.2.3`, `>=1.2.3`, `<1.2.3`, `<=1.2.3`: comparisons. A partial version counts as
  its range, so `=1.2` means `>=1.2.0, <1.3.0` and `>1.2` means `>=1.3.0`.
- `1.*`, `1.2.*`, or `*` alone: wildcards, also spelled with `x` or `X`.

Spaces can come before and after each comparator and after an operator.

#### Errors

- `SemverError` with the reason and byte offset of the first problem:
  - `Empty` for empty text or text of only spaces.
  - `UnexpectedCharacter` for a byte that is not valid there, such as a missing comma, a `v`
    prefix, `||`, a hyphen range, or `*` together with other comparators.
  - `UnexpectedEnd`, `LeadingZero`, `NumberTooLarge`, or `EmptyIdentifier` for a bad version.
  - `TooManyComparators` for more than 32 comparators, which Cargo also rejects.

#### Gotchas

A bare version means `^`, so `1.2.3` matches `1.9.0`. Write `=1.2.3` for exactly one version.

<a id="VersionRange.impl.matches"></a>

### Method `matches`

```silk
pub fn matches(self: &Self, version: &Version<'_>) -> bool
```

Returns `true` if `version` is in the range.

#### Details

A pre-release version matches only if it is in the range and a comparator in the same
alternative names a pre-release with the same `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. So `>=1.2.3-alpha` matches
`1.2.3-beta` but not `1.2.4-beta`, and `^1.2.3` matches no pre-release. Build metadata of
`version` does not count.

<a id="VersionRange.impl.matchesIncludingPrerelease"></a>

### Method `matchesIncludingPrerelease`

```silk
pub fn matchesIncludingPrerelease(self: &Self, version: &Version<'_>) -> bool
```

Returns `true` if `version` is in the range, with pre-releases treated as other versions.

#### Details

For an npm range, this is the `includePrerelease` option of the `semver` package: the bounds
of `^`, `~`, `x`, and hyphen ranges include their pre-releases, so `^1.2.3` matches
`1.4.0-beta` and `1.x` matches `1.0.0-rc.1`. For a Cargo range, only the rule that a
pre-release needs a comparator with a pre-release of the same `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` is dropped.
Build metadata of `version` does not count.

<a id="VersionRange.impl.bestMatch"></a>

### Method `bestMatch`

```silk
pub fn bestMatch(self: &Self, versions: &[Version<'_>]) -> Option<usize>
```

Returns the position of the highest version in `versions` that the range matches, or `None`.

#### Details

Matching uses [`VersionRange.matches`](#VersionRange.impl.matches), so pre-releases match only by that rule. Versions
compare by precedence and then build metadata, and the first of two equal versions wins.
